newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends higher, gilt prices steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends higher, gilt prices steady.

text.p: Indian call money ended Wednesday at 9.50-9.75 percent, slightly up from the day's opening levels of 9.0-9.50 percent, dealers said.

Most of the day's deals were done in the 9.25-9.50 percent range, they said. "Towards the end of the day, some lenders seemed to be off the market," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "This pushed up rates slightly."

He said some banks seemed to have built up large positions in government securities, anticipating a cut in cash reserves in the monetary policy to be announced on October 19. This would lead to lower interest rates and a rise in bond prices, he said.
"Banks are punting on a fall in interest rates and building up positions in securities hoping to cash in later," he said.
"But maybe too much money has gone into such trading... the availability of funds for call operations seems to have been affected thanks to this diversion to securities."
Dealers said trading volume in the secondary market for government securities fell on Wednesday to 1.01 billion rupees from 2.13 billion on Tuesday. Prices were steady, they said.
"Banks are pulling back a bit," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Positions have been taken and now the market will await the monetary policy announcement."
There were no trades in certificates of deposit and commercial paper on Wednesday, dealers said.
Dealers said rates on intercorporate deposits remained unchanged in the 18-20 percent range for top-rated borrowers.
